newsitem.title: FRANCE: Mobutu meets UN envoy, to return home soon.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu meets UN envoy, to return home soon.

text.p: Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko discussed the situation in eastern Zaire with United Nations special envoy Raymond Chretien on Wednesday.
Chretien visited Mobutu at his French Riviera villa after the 66-year-old Zairean president, recuperating from prostate cancer surgery, made a brief appearance before a handful of reporters.
The U.N. envoy made no comment after the meeting but said he would hold a news conference later in the day.
Mobutu, who has been away from Zaire since August, did not speak to the reporters. But Zairean ambassador to France Baya Ramazini said he was getting better and would soon return home.
"The president will go back home in the next few days. The situation demands it," he told the reporters invited in to the villa to see Mobutu.
Mobutu had been undergoing treatment for his cancer in Switzerland but left Lausanne for his sprawling luxury French Riviera villa on Monday.

He has remained silent since fighting broke out in his country between Zairean troops and Rwandan-backed Tutsi rebels, trapping more than one million starving refugees and threatening the government's hold on northeastern Zaire.
"The president is getting much better but he is still convalescing and has resumed a bit of activity in light of the situation in his country," Ramazini said.
He said Mobutu was following developments back in Zaire through regular contacts with senior government officials including Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo.
All government actions were taken in agreement with the president, he said.

Chretien told reporters on his arrival at Nice airport late on Tuesday night that Mobutu had been the "guarantor of the security of his country for many decades...He has been an active president who was always in control when he was in Kinshasa".
Chretien, Canada's ambassador to the United States, planned to fly later to Kinshasa for talks with the Zairean prime minister.
Mobutu arrived in France on Monday from Switzerland for a few days' stay at his pink and white marble villa near Nice after undergoing surgery in Lausanne in August.

At a summit in Nairobi on Tuesday, eight African nations urged the United Nations to arrange a "neutral" protection force to come to the rescue of a million abandoned refugees in Zaire, but volunteers for the force appeared sparse.
A Spanish Foreign Ministry spokesman said that Spain and France favoured sending a multinational force of at least 5,000 troops to enable relief supplies to get through to the refugees.
French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette said there was six months' supply of food within 1,000 km (625 miles) of the refugee camps.
